device.description: 12-bit octal-channel ultralow-glitch voltage-output DAC with 50 MHz SPI interface (24-bit word), four reference inputs, IOVDD level shifters, daisy-chain SDO, RSTSEL-selected binary/two's complement coding and asynchronous reset
device.note: dac7558.pdf (SLAS435A) p.4 power requirements (VDD, IOVDD 2.7-5.5 V; IOVDD down to 1.8 V, note 1), p.5 timing characteristics and serial write operation (Figure 1), p.6-7 pin description (RHB) and terminal functions, p.18 serial interface programming (Table 1), p.19 power-on reset, p.20 power down (Tables 2-3, PD pin), asynchronous clear (RST, RSTSEL), input data format, 24-bit word, p.21 SYNC (the SYNC rising edge after the 24th bit updates the DACs with DCEN low), daisy chain

pages: p.4 (supplies), p.5 (timing, Figure 1), p.6-7 (pins), p.18 (Table 1), p.19 (power-on reset), p.20 (power down, Tables 2-3, RST/RSTSEL, data format, 24-bit word), p.21 (SYNC, daisy chain)
notModeled: analog outputs, references and VFB sense inputs (never driven)
RSTSEL selects straight binary (low) or two's complement (high) coding, so reset/RST code 0 is zero scale or mid scale; registers store the code as written and RSTSEL is a plain input
PD pin low powers down all channels to Hi-Z and resumes the previous state when high (p.20): outputs are never driven, so it is a plain input
power-down output loads: stored per channel in PWR only; how a powered-down channel returns to normal operation is not described
daisy-chain mode (DCEN high): SDO repeating SDIN with a 24-clock delay and latching the last 24 bits at SYNC rising are not modeled; SDO stays Hi-Z (the DCEN-low behavior)
A1 A0 (DB23-DB22) other than 00: the DAC does not respond (no command matches)
RST: the DAC updates at the first SYNC rising edge after RST returns high (p.20); modeled as reset held while RST is low
SCLK limits (50 MHz, 10 MHz with SDO) and setup/hold times
variants: octal member of the DAC7551/DAC7552/DAC7558 family (daisy-chainable together).
